findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD.

A tray of raw ground beef is observed stored on a shelf over containers of cooked ground beef used for sandwiches in the reach in cooler across from the hand washing station. The PIC was shown and rearranged the items during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that foods are stored so that cross contamination of pathogens is not a concern.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle used for root beer on the fountain drink machine is observed heavily soiled on the inner surface during his inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned the nozzle during this inspection to correct. He stated that they are soaked regularly. This helps but routine cleaning is still needed to maintain safe standards. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-303.11 Ice Used as Exterior Coolant, Prohibited as Ingredient. After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD. 

A gallon of tea is observed stored in the ice in the ice machine during this inspection. The PIC was shown and removed the item during this inspection to correct. Ensure that ice used for drinks is not used as a cooling or cold holding medium.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Allergen training is not available for the certified food protection manager (CFPM) during this inspection. This situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to renew prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

Wet wiping cloths are observed on the counters throughout the kitchen. There is a CL smell to the cloths indicating that they are used for sanitizing. This was discussed with the PIC and they moved the cloths back to the bucket to correct. Ensure that all wiping cloths used in the kitchen are stored between uses in solution at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink used for the kitchen was without paper towels. The PIC was notified and the towels were replaced during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Raw ground beef is observed over cooked beef and pickles in the refrigerator in the back. The PIC moved the items during the inspection to correct. Do not store raw meats over Ready-To-Eat foods in the coolers.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle of the root beer on the fountain drink machine is observed soiled. PIC indicated that they soak/clean the item weekly. This needs to take place more often. The item was cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that it is cleaned often enough to prevent accumulation of slime/mold.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Raw ground beef is observed over cooked beef and pickles in the refrigerator in the back. The PIC moved the items as the inspector was looking at them. Violation corrected immediately.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 

The ice scoop is observed soiled on the handle and is in need of cleaning. The PIC was shown and the scoop washed during the inspection to correct.
